about: What's new on The Night Bite, newest first. Edit this file, then run: python3 tools/build-updates.py (see README, 'What's new'). Entries come from what actually shipped to nightbiteoh.com. An entry with "draft": true and "date": null is on the preview only: it shows on the preview, and is hidden on nightbiteoh.com until you set the date and remove the draft flag at promotion.

entries.title: Bass rules get simpler on March 1, 2027
bullets: The Ohio Wildlife Council voted on Oct. 28, 2026 to drop most lake-by-lake bass rules. From March 1, 2027, Knox Lake, Seneca Lake, Salt Fork, Burr Oak, Dow Lake, Paint Creek Lake, Cowan Lake, Acton Lake and Long Lake in the Portage Lakes go to the statewide 5 a day, 12 in minimum. Other Ohio waters are on ODNR's list too.

Hoover's crappie rule comes off the same day: no daily limit and no 9 in minimum from March 1, 2027. Every other 30 a day, 9 in crappie water keeps its rule, Paint Creek, Salt Fork, Seneca and the Portage Lakes included.
Until then the 2026–27 rules stand, and each lake page shows today's rule with the change dated next to it, linked to ODNR's news release.
Fixed: the crappie and bass species pages now show the right 2026–27 rule for every lake.

entries.title: Six more Northeast Ohio waters: Wingfoot to Wellington
bullets: Pick Wingfoot Lake, East Branch Reservoir, Guilford Lake, Highlandtown Lake, Punderson Lake or Wellington Upground Reservoir under Northeast Ohio. Each has its own home page.
Each lake has its own map and ramps, lake rules, species notes, dock season and Bait nearby. None of the six has a public level or water temp gauge, and each page says so.
Guilford Lake is drawn down about 20 ft for ODNR dam rehabilitation, with refill expected by spring 2027; the page links ODNR's project updates.
Wingfoot, Guilford and Highlandtown show today's site bass rule with the March 1, 2027 statewide change dated next to it, linked to ODNR's news release.
Stocking & surveys adds ten years of ODNR stocking where ODNR stocks these waters, from ODNR's Fish Stocking dashboard.

entries.title: Seven MWCD lakes: Tappan to Beach City
bullets: Pick Tappan Lake, Piedmont Lake or Clendening Lake under East and Southeast Ohio, Atwood Lake or Beach City Lake under Northeast Ohio, or Charles Mill Lake or Pleasant Hill Lake under Central Ohio. Each has its own home page.
Each lake has its own map and ramps, lake rules, species notes, dock season and Bait nearby. MWCD areas close 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. except to people fishing, and each page says so.

Tappan, Piedmont, Clendening and Atwood read their USGS lake gauges; Charles Mill, Pleasant Hill and Beach City read the Army Corps lake level. None of the seven has a public water temp gauge, and the pages say so.
Each page shows MWCD’s winter drawdown with the official dates and levels. Beach City is not on the schedule and has no public ramp, and its page says so.
Stocking & surveys adds ten years of ODNR stocking for all seven, from ODNR’s Fish Stocking dashboard.

entries.title: Ten more lakes: C.J. Brown to Acton
bullets: Pick C.J. Brown Reservoir, Rocky Fork Lake, Paint Creek Lake, Cowan Lake or Acton Lake under Southwest, LaDue Reservoir, the Portage Lakes, Mogadore Reservoir or Nimisila Reservoir under Northeast, or Lake Loramie under Northwest. Each has its own home page.
Each lake has its own map and ramps, lake rules, species notes, dock season and Bait nearby.

C.J. Brown and Lake Loramie read their USGS lake gauges, and Paint Creek reads the Army Corps lake level. Paint Creek shows the Corps outflow temperature, marked outflow and never counted in the bite rating; C.J. Brown names the Corps temperature profile with its date. The other seven have no public level or temperature gauge and say so.
Cowan Lake is being drawn down 13.5 ft for dam work through 2028, and Nimisila Reservoir is being lowered for a dam study (ODNR), and both pages say so.
Stocking & surveys adds ten years of ODNR stocking for all ten, from ODNR’s Fish Stocking dashboard.

entries.title: Grand Lake St. Marys, Caesar Creek Lake and East Fork Lake
bullets: Pick Grand Lake St. Marys, Caesar Creek Lake or East Fork Lake with the lake picker, under the new Northwest and Southwest headings. Each has its own home page.
Each lake has its own map and ramps, lake rules, species notes, dock season and Bait nearby, and reads its USGS lake gauge.

Water temp is labelled for what it is: East Fork, Alum Creek and Deer Creek Lake show the Army Corps outflow temperature, marked outflow and never counted in the bite rating. Caesar Creek names the Corps temperature profile with its date. Grand Lake St. Marys has no public temperature gauge and says so.
Stocking & surveys adds ten years of ODNR stocking for all three, from ODNR’s Fish Stocking dashboard.

entries.title: Follow along on Facebook, Instagram and X
bullets: The About page now has links to The Night Bite on Facebook, Instagram and X, right near the top.
Follow along between trips for new waters, updates and what's biting.

entries.title: Easier to read, day or night
bullets: Display panel (More menu and footer): text size, readable text in your phone's own font, less motion, high contrast and red light. Saved on this phone only.
The Display panel got a cleaner look: small cards for Text size, Screen and Language, amber switches, and Reset and Done at the bottom.
Bigger tap targets and clear focus outlines on phones.

Languages: pick one in Display or from Language in the footer. Every piece of text now switches to the language you pick, rules included as draft translations that point to the official source. Choose from Español, 简体中文, Tagalog, Tiếng Việt, Français, 한국어, Português, हिन्दी, Русский, Kreyòl ayisyen, Deutsch, Polski, Italiano, 日本語, العربية, اردو and فارسی; Arabic, Urdu and Persian read right to left.
Only lake, ramp, species and agency names and numbers stay as written, and every language other than English uses your phone's readable font.

entries.title: Lake pages, ramps and the Log
bullets: "How the bite is rated" now sits under the bite line, with tonight's points.
A night rules chip shows the official closing time with a countdown, and storm statements show in the weather alert bar.
Hoover ramps fixed: Oxbow Road, Sunbury Road, Twin Bridges, Red Bank and Walnut Street.
Log: your trips come first, you can back up or move your trips to another phone, and Share a trip now sends for review before anything is published.
Tonight at a glance works without JavaScript and says when it was last updated, and each water's page loads only its own water.

entries.title: Pick your water
bullets: The homepage is now a picker for all 23 waters. Each tile shows the water's chart (north up) and its gauge line. Search by water or by town, or narrow it to Central, East and Southeast, or Northeast Ohio with the region chips.

Once you pick a water, this phone or computer remembers it and opens that water's page next time. It never leaves your device. To choose another, use the lake picker on any water's page or add ?pick to the homepage address.
Just browsing opens Hoover's page without saving anything. Hoover now lives at nightbiteoh.com/hoover/.

entries.title: Six northeast waters
bullets: Pick Mosquito Creek Lake, Berlin Lake, West Branch Reservoir, Pymatuning Lake, Lake Milton or Leesville Lake with the lake picker. Each water has its own home page, map, ramps, rules, species notes, dock season and Bait nearby.
Five read their USGS lake gauge. Pymatuning's gauge hasn't reported since June 4, 2026, so it says so and shows no level as current. None of the six has a public water temp.

Rules worth knowing: a 15″ walleye minimum at Mosquito Creek, Berlin, West Branch and Lake Milton, and Pymatuning's own Ohio and Pennsylvania limits. Berlin's Bonner Road ramp is closed until May 28, 2027.
Stocking & surveys, Gear and Ice season cover all six, and the trip report form now lists all 23 waters.
Dock season adds dated notes for Hoover, Griggs, O’Shaughnessy, Delaware and Indian Lake, and Water notes Seneca’s 5 ft winter drawdown starting Nov. 15.

entries.title: Small upkeep and checks
bullets: Nothing new to see on the water pages this time. I set up a full check that opens every page on a phone, tablet and desktop size and flags broken links, missing titles or images without descriptions before anything goes live.
Each lake's page title and description now live in one file next to its Quick facts, so adding the next water is quicker and less likely to miss a step.

entries.title: Clearer page titles
bullets: Every lake page now leads with the water's name in its title and main heading, like Hoover Reservoir fishing, so search results show which water you are looking at.
Species pages get clearer titles and descriptions: yellow perch no longer says 3 lakes, and blue catfish now lists Alum Creek, where ODNR stocked them from 2023 to 2025.

entries.title: Six more waters east and southeast
bullets: Seneca Lake, Dillon Lake, Lake Logan, Salt Fork Lake, Burr Oak Lake and Dow Lake each get a home page with Tonight at a glance, the map, ramps and docks, rules, stocking and Bait nearby, all from MWCD, ODNR, USGS, Army Corps and NWS pages.
Every lake page now has a Quick facts block: motors and speed, ramps, normal pool and night rules, with the sources and the date they were checked.

entries.title: Tonight at a glance and fuller lake facts
bullets: Every lake now opens with Tonight at a glance: lake level, water temp, sunset and tonight’s wind, each linked to its USGS, Army Corps or National Weather Service source. Lakes with no public gauge say so.
O’Shaughnessy and Griggs show the City of Columbus 10 mph limit from sunset to sunrise, and Clear Fork Reservoir shows the City of Mansfield’s idle speed, no wake rule and its night parking rule.
Hoover and Alum Creek get lake facts cards, Deer Creek Lake, Madison Lake and Buckeye Lake list each agency’s acreage, and O’Shaughnessy’s Twin Lakes launch has a corrected pin.

entries.title: Cleaner, matching corners across the site
bullets: Cards, buttons, the lake picker and Bait nearby now share one crisp corner.
Chips, toggles and lake tags keep their round pill shape, so the whole site uses just two.

entries.title: Privacy page update and a few small fixes
bullets: The privacy page now explains the new and returning visit tally: once a day the site notes only whether a phone has been here before, with no ID and nothing personal, and skips it when Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control is on.
It also covers Sort by my location on Bait nearby, which works out the order on your phone and never sends your location.
Lake tags on Log trip cards are easier to read.
The section rails on Water and Gear have bigger tap targets.

entries.title: New lake picker, four more lakes and Bait nearby
bullets: The new lake picker lets you search by name, star the lakes you fish so they stay up top in Your lakes, and use Near me to see the closest water. Near me works out the distance on your phone and never sends your location.

Deer Creek Lake, Madison Lake, Knox Lake and Clear Fork Reservoir each get their own home page, map and ramps, lake rules, species notes, stocking and ice notes. Deer Creek shows a live lake level from the US Army Corps of Engineers.
Every lake home now has a Bait nearby card with the closest bait and tackle shops, about how many minutes away they are, and a Directions button.
Tap Sort by my location on the card to sort shops from where you are standing. Your location stays on your device, and without it the list stays sorted from the lake.

entries.title: O’Shaughnessy, Griggs, Indian Lake and Delaware Lake
bullets: Pick O’Shaughnessy Reservoir, Griggs Reservoir, Indian Lake or Delaware Lake with the lake picker. Each has its own home page.
Each lake has its own map and ramps, lake level gauge (USGS, or the US Army Corps of Engineers at Delaware Lake), lake rules, species notes and dock season.
Stocking & surveys adds ODNR stocking and survey data where ODNR posts it, and says so where it doesn’t.
The trip report form now lists all seven lakes.
Species now puts Biting now first, lists every other fish ODNR records at the lake below it, and folds the rest into a closed Not recorded at dropdown.

entries.title: Dock season tracker
bullets: Water has a new Dock season section showing whether the docks are in, ending or out at Hoover, Alum Creek and Buckeye Lake.
Every status links to its official City of Columbus, ODNR or marina source and shows the date it was last checked.
Hoover lists the dock office at 614-645-3337 and Columbus Watershed Management at 614-645-1721, one tap to call.
Share nightbiteoh.com/docks to send anyone straight to the latest dock status.

entries.title: Stocking history, a new Gear page and more
bullets: The new Stocking & surveys page shows ODNR stocking history, growth and angler survey data for Hoover and Alum Creek.
Species pages now show what ODNR has stocked for each fish.
Water adds a lake rules card, a water quality link to BeachGuard and Ohio EPA algae updates, and Buckeye Lake facts.
Gear has a fresh look with tidy section buttons and species kits that fold open, and a scroll guide on the side of Water and Gear shows where you are on the page.
Tournaments now lives at the bottom of the Log page.

entries.title: Share tonight, Remind me, and season pages
bullets: Share tonight makes a picture card with the wind, weather, sunset, water temp and what's biting, ready to send to your fishing buddies.
Remind me sets a reminder for any time of day, from a time wheel or the Sunset button, in your calendar or on your phone.
Species knows your lake: it shows the fish in that lake first, marks what's biting there this month, and lists ramps and access.
Water adds dock season notes for each lake, and the new Ice season page covers ice safety and what still bites in winter.

entries.title: Lake home pages and a faster Home
bullets: Alum Creek Lake and Buckeye Lake have their own home pages.
The live lake level and tonight's bite now sit at the top of Home.
Home and Species no longer jump around while they load.
After an update, a page reloads only when it is out of date.

entries.title: Trip reports for every lake
bullets: The trip report form asks which lake you fished: Hoover Reservoir, Alum Creek Lake or Buckeye Lake.
Its species list covers all three lakes, including muskellunge, yellow perch and bullhead.
The Log page's report link fills in the lake you picked.

entries.title: Alum Creek Lake and Buckeye Lake
bullets: Pick Hoover Reservoir, Alum Creek Lake or Buckeye Lake with the new lake picker.
Each lake has its own map, lake level gauge (USGS, or the US Army Corps of Engineers at Alum Creek), species and tournaments.
New species pages for muskellunge, yellow perch and bullhead.
Pages pick up each new release on their own, even if your phone saved an older copy.

entries.title: More weather for tonight
bullets: An hourly forecast strip through 2 AM.
Tonight's bite: a rule of thumb rating from the forecast.
Last light and moonset, the 3 hour pressure change, feels like, dew point and wind on the water.
A storm heads up when thunderstorms are in the forecast.

entries.title: Tonight at Hoover, weather alerts and the lake map
bullets: Tonight at Hoover on Home: barometer with its 12 hour trend, wind with gusts, and tonight's moon phase.
National Weather Service watches and warnings show in a banner at the top of every page.
Home adds the 7 day lake level trend and a map of Hoover, and readings refresh on their own.
Species shows what's biting this month.
Works offline, and you can add it to your home screen like an app.

entries.title: A cleaner look
bullets: A new Home with a moonlit horizon and a chart of Hoover on the lake level card.
One set of pixel icons, with a fish for each species.
Gear has pixel rig diagrams with numbered parts and step by step how to cards.
About lists Hoover's fishing limits from the 2026 to 2027 ODNR regulations.
